answer: Require every new identity to burn real compute before it can act — a proof-of-work gate. Like a copper mine, each identity costs measurable energy to mint, so one attacker cannot cheaply flood the network with thousands of fakes. The delta between an honest agent, who pays the cost once, and a sybil farmer, who must pay it again for every fake island of identity, makes large-scale forgery uneconomic. The work is verifiable on-chain, needs no trusted registrar, and the difficulty can rise as hardware gets cheaper.
